Step-by-step full example

Source: vignettes/Step_By_Step_Full_Example.Rmd
Step_By_Step_Full_Example.Rmd

This tutorial walks through the main operating modes of gcamsdg (which supports both GCAM and GCAM-Europe databases). Note: We highly recommend reading the Before Starting section and Example 1 first. Foundational concepts are explained in detail there, whereas subsequent examples assume you are already familiar with those basics to avoid repetition.

The walkthrough covers: processing a single database (Example 1), handling several separate policy-scenario databases (Example 2), using a single project file (Example 3), specifying multiple project files (Example 4), pairing the tool with a standard gcamreport run (Example 5), and selecting specific SDGs to generate basic figures (Example 6). For the complete parameter list, run ?generate_sdg_report in your console or consult the reference index.

Before starting: load the gcamsdg package

  1. Install the package (see the README):
devtools::install_github("bc3LC/gcamsdg")
  1. Load it. If you are using RStudio working directly on a clone, run
devtools::load_all()

and otherwise

library(gcamsdg)

newline

Example 1: compute SDG indicators form a single database

Once the package is installed and your GCAM or GCAM-Europe database is ready, run generate_sdg_report() by specifying the db_path and db_name arguments:

result <- generate_sdg_report(
  db_path = "/path/to/my/databases",        # path to the database
  db_name = "my_gcam_database",             # extension added automatically if missing
  desired_scen = c("scen1", "scen2"),       # omit to use every scenario in the database
  sdgs = "all"                              # run `available_sdgs()` to see the options
  final_db_year = 2050                      # defaults to 2100. Indicate otherwise
)

Behind the scenes this creates an rgcam project via create_prj(), which reads all the SDG queries bundled with the package (gcamsdg::query_file) plus a couple of heavier queries added only when needed (detailed land allocation for "land" and nonCO2 emissions by sector for "health"); then computes each requested indicator.

Check the individual results: The function returns a named list containing one data frame per requested SDG (e.g., result$gdp, result$water), which is automatically saved to your local drive as output/<output_name>_resultSDGs.RData. Simultaneously, the raw CSV data for each indicator is exported to dedicated subfolders based on the SDG module (e.g., SDG1-GDP, SDG6-Water) located under output/<SDG>/indiv_results/.

Review the consolidated report: The function binds these individual metrics together into a single, standardized dataset, which is saved automatically as a comprehensive CSV & RData file at output/<output_name>_reportSDGs.csv and output/<output_name>_reportSDGs.RData.

newline

Example 2: compute SDG indicators from several policy-scenario databases

In large scenario ensembles, each policy is typically stored in its own separate GCAM database. To process multiple databases simultaneously, pass a vector of database names to the db_name argument (and optionally, an output_name to customize the output (generated project and SDG estimates) prefixes). generate_sdg_report() will automatically extract and compute the requested sdgs for each one. Note: The function evaluates every possible combination of db_path and db_name. To avoid unintended paths, store all target databases in the same directory and provide a single path string for db_path.

result <- generate_sdg_report(
  db_path = "/path/to/my/databases",        # path to the database
  db_name = c("database_basexdb_policyA",   # extension added automatically if missing
              "database_basexdb_policyB", 
              "database_basexdb_policyC"),
  sdgs = "all",                             # run `available_sdgs()` to see the options
  final_db_year = 2050                      # defaults to 2100. Indicate otherwise
)

The function generates a combined project file stored at output/<output_name>.dat, alongside the computed SDG metrics and the standardized comprehensive dataset, as shown in Example 1.

newline

Example 3: compute SDG indicators from a single project file

In case you already hold the project file (with all the required queries to compute the desired SDGs), you can directly indicate its path via prj_name. The project will be loaded and the SDGs computed:

result <- generate_sdg_report(
  prj_name = "/path/and/name/to/my/GCAMproject",  # extension added automatically if missing
  sdgs = "all",                                   # run `available_sdgs()` to see the options
  final_db_year = 2050                            # defaults to 2100. Indicate otherwise
)

newline

Example 4: compute SDG indicators from several project files

In case your scenarios are scattered across several project files, the function loads them, selecting only the desired scenarios, and creates a single project file (save at output/<output_name>.dat) before computing the SDGs:

result <- generate_sdg_report(
  prj_name = c("/path/to/prjA.dat",
               "/path/to/prjB.dat",
               "/path/to/prjC.dat"),        # extension added automatically if missing
  output_name = "desired_name",             # prjA name considered if missing
  sdgs = "all",                             # run `available_sdgs()` to see the options
  final_db_year = 2050                      # defaults to 2100. Indicate otherwise
)

newline

Example 5: compute SDG indicators producing also the standard gcamreport output

If you also want the standard gcamreport IPCC-style output from the same project (instead of extracting the database a second time) and taking advantage of all the SDG variables already computed by this tool, set run_gcamreport = TRUE and provide GCAM_version. You can also specify other gcamreport::generate_report() variables via gcamreport_args:

result <- generate_sdg_report(
  db_path = "/path/to/my/databases",      # path to the database
  db_name = "my_gcam_database"            # extension added automatically if missing
  sdgs = "all",                           # run `available_sdgs()` to see the options
  run_gcamreport = TRUE, 
  GCAM_version = "vEurope7.2",            # run `gcamreport::available_GCAM_versions()` to see the options
  final_db_year = 2050                    # defaults to 2100. Indicate otherwise
)
result$gcamreport                         # gcamreport's standardized output

This requires the gcamreport package (devtools::install_github("bc3LC/gcamreport")). Currently, the function supports only a single database input (db_name), although it can accept an array of pre-existing project files.

newline

Example 6: compute SDG indicators and produce basic figures

Set makeFigures = TRUE to also generate a basic PNG per computed indicator:

result <- generate_sdg_report(
  db_path = "/path/to/my/databases",        # path to the database
  db_name = "my_gcam_database"              # extension added automatically if missing
  sdgs = c("gdp", "poverty", "water"),      # run `available_sdgs()` to see the options
  final_db_year = 2050,                     # defaults to 2100. Indicate otherwise
  makeFigures = TRUE
)

Each PNG is saved alongside that indicator’s other output, under output/figures/ (e.g. .../SDG1-GDP_<output_name>.png). The figures are simple scenario-colored time series line charts for indicators with a year dimension, or a bar chart by scenario for SDG15’s PSL (a single net 2020-2050 value, no year dimension). Regional indicators (population, GDP, health) are aggregated to one global series first, water indicators are depicted by region.
